name: Stanislaus Petrov-Adeyemi
role: Vultures crew chief / freelance trauma surgeon
description:
Stash runs a Vultures crew out of the south Pulaski sub-tier. The Vultures, per existing canon, are the body-pickup-after-shootouts operation that doubles as organ-repossession technicians (see project_vultures memory). Stash's crew is one of the four crews that work the GLMZ corridor. His specific reputation is for keeping the body alive a little longer than the body should reasonably stay alive — long enough for the organs to be paired with their next host without the freezer process degrading the tissue. The technique is not, strictly speaking, on the side of medicine. It is also not, strictly speaking, illegal in any of the jurisdictions Stash operates in, which is a fact he has examined closely.

Kyle has worked with Stash twice: once when Stash needed muscle for a body-pickup that turned hostile, once when Stash arranged Kyle's own delivery to Hua's south-arm chamber as a corpse via False Death Protocol (canon: Street Meat / A Borrowed Hand). They are not friends. They respect each other. Stash has not yet asked Kyle for a third favor, which Kyle reads as Stash holding the favor in reserve, which Kyle suspects is exactly right.
heritage: Slavic-Yoruba. Father's family from Kursk via the Ukrainian climate wars. Mother's family from Ibadan via the Lagos Pulse hub. Stash speaks Russian, Yoruba, and English — the three languages used in business at the south Pulaski Vultures depot.
specialty: emergency trauma stabilization on bodies that ought to be dead; organ-recovery surgical work; body-disposal logistics; the False Death Protocol delivery (one of three known operators who can run it cleanly)
method: runs a four-person crew (two technicians, one driver, one armed escort). Stash himself does the surgical work. He does not enjoy it. He does not stop, either. He has not had a steady night of sleep since 2218.
code: the body the Vultures pick up is the body the Vultures own, and what the Vultures do with it is the Vultures' business. He does not extract organs from the unwilling. He does extract organs from the contractually-obligated. The difference, by his own admission, is sometimes negotiated rather than discovered.
signature_gear: a Helix Biosystems portable autodoc in the back of his Vultures van; a surgical pack he has refined over fifteen years that has a place for every instrument and is set up the same way every time so he can work in the dark; a heavy-frame revolver he wears on the right hip and has fired four times; the standard Vultures-issue tracker badge that grants him access to corponation morgue facilities under the freelance-cleanup framework agreement
relationship_to_kyle: working, not personal. Stash respects Kyle because Kyle paid him without complaint for the Street Meat delivery even though the delivery nearly killed Kyle. Kyle respects Stash because Stash kept Kyle alive on the slab when Stash had no contractual obligation to. They have a balance. Neither of them is sure who owes whom, which is the most stable kind of balance two operators can have.
aesthetic: mid-fifties, broad-shouldered, the build of a man who used to lift things for a living and now lifts smaller things more carefully. Always in scrubs under his coat. Always smells of antiseptic. The Vultures patch is on his left sleeve.
spin_off_hook: A body the Vultures pick up turns out to be carrying an unauthorized organ pairing the corponation database does not know about. The pairing implicates someone Stash has been doing business with for years. He has to decide whether to file the pairing into the official record (which closes the Vultures contract cleanly and burns the contact) or alter the record (which keeps the contact and exposes Stash to a level of legal risk he has spent fifteen years avoiding). Kyle gets pulled in as the only freelancer Stash trusts to make a delivery to a third party Stash cannot be seen meeting with.
